MP4 is lossy. It's nice for consumer grade applications, but formats like .avi prove their usefullness in professional applications, because they are lossless. Lossless is important for editing video: lossless files will not decrease in quality as they are edited; lossy files will.

As for why older codecs are used, the reasons are typically going to by either legacy compatibility (some proprietary device x only supports mp2 video) or political (someone might prefer using an open source codec even if it is slightly worse).
